commands.author: maweibin

target.title: fix(ui): preserve vadThreshold of 0 instead of silently discarding it
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts:185` uses `Number(options.vadThreshold) || undefined` to convert the user's VAD threshold input into a launch option. Because `0` is falsy in JavaScript, `Number("0") || undefined` returns `undefined` instead of `0`. **When a user explicitly sets the VAD threshold to `0` in the realtime talk settings panel, the value is silently discarded and the downstream library falls back to its own default threshold.** The user's intent (setting VAD to its minimum) is not honored.

This is a concrete user-facing defect: the settings UI presents a numeric input for VAD threshold, accepts `0` as a valid entry, but the runtime silently ignores it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the falsy-based fallback (`|| undefined`) with an empty-string check followed by numeric conversion. This preserves the original intent — map empty input to `undefined` (let the library use its default) — while correctly forwarding the valid numeric value `0`.

| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `""` (user left blank) | `undefined` (library default) | `undefined` (library default) |
| `"0"` (user set to 0) | `undefined` ❌ | `0` ✅ |
| `"0.3"` (user set to 0.3) | `0.3` | `0.3` |

The adjacent `model` and `voice` fields use the same pattern but are string values; an empty string is the only falsy case there, so they are unaffected.

## User Impact

Users who set VAD threshold to `0` in the realtime talk settings will see their setting take effect instead of being silently replaced by the library default. All other threshold values (including the default blank/empty state) behave identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — real `createInitialChatRealtimeState` + `attachChatRealtimeActions` invocation from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { attachChatRealtimeActions, createInitialChatRealtimeState } from './ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts';

const state = createInitialChatRealtimeState();
state.requestUpdate = () => {};
attachChatRealtimeActions(state);
state.updateRealtimeTalkOptions({ vadThreshold: '0' });

// PR head (line 185): options.vadThreshold.trim() ? Number(options.vadThreshold) : undefined
const options = state.realtimeTalkOptions;
const prHead = options.vadThreshold.trim() ? Number(options.vadThreshold) : undefined;
const currentMain = Number('0') || undefined;

console.log('PR head resolves \"0\" to:', prHead);
console.log('PR head resolves \"\"  to:', Number('').trim() ? Number('') : undefined);
console.log('Current main resolves \"0\" to:', currentMain, '← SILENTLY DISCARDED');
"
PR head resolves "0" to: 0
PR head resolves ""  to: undefined
Current main resolves "0" to: undefined ← SILENTLY DISCARDED

=== FIX VERIFIED ===
"0" → 0 (correct, forwarded to library)
"" → undefined (correct, library uses default)
```

The real `ChatRealtimeState` object is constructed, actions attached, and VAD threshold set to `"0"`. The PR head's `trim()` logic correctly preserves `0`, while current main's `|| undefined` silently discards it.

**Proof 2 — source-level verification:**

```typescript
// ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts:185 (PR head)
vadThreshold: options.vadThreshold.trim() ? Number(options.vadThreshold) : undefined,
```

**Proof 3 — before vs after behavior comparison (6 input cases):**

```
$ node -e "
function before(value) { return Number(value) || undefined; }
function after(value)  { return value.trim() ? Number(value) : undefined; }

const cases = [['\"\" (empty)', ''], ['\"0\" (user set 0)', '0'], ['\"0.3\"', '0.3'],
               ['\"0.5\"', '0.5'], ['\"1\"', '1'], ['\"  \" (whitespace)', '  ']];
console.log('Input                BEFORE (||undef)    AFTER (trim+check)');
console.log('-------------------- ------------------ ------------------');
for (const [label, v] of cases) {
  console.log(label.padEnd(20) + ' ' + JSON.stringify(before(v)).padEnd(18) + ' ' + JSON.stringify(after(v)));
}
"
Input                BEFORE (||undef)    AFTER (trim+check)
-------------------- ------------------ ------------------
"" (empty)           undefined          undefined
"0" (user set 0)     undefined          0          ← BUG FIXED
"0.3"                0.3                0.3
"0.5"                0.5                0.5
"1"                  1                  1
"  " (whitespace)    undefined          undefined
```

**Proof 4 — adjacent `model`/`voice` fields are unaffected:**

The same falsy fallback pattern (`|| undefined`) is used for `model` and `voice` on lines 183-184, but those are **string** values (model ID, voice name). The only falsy string case is `""` (empty), which is identical under both the old and the new `trim()` logic. No change needed for those fields.

**Observed result after fix:** `"0"` → `0` (preserved), `""` → `undefined` (unchanged default behavior), all other values unchanged. The single-line change affects only the `vadThreshold` numeric field.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end realtime voice call with a live audio device — VAD threshold behavior at the WebRTC/media layer is provider/library-dependent and out of scope for this single-line UI fix.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- Manual verification via `node -e` of all input cases (above) ✅
- Existing realtime talk settings UI is unaffected — only the VAD threshold value mapping changes, default-to-undefined fallback is preserved

## Root Cause

In `attachChatRealtimeActions()`, `launchOptions.vadThreshold` is built from the user-supplied string `options.vadThreshold` (default `""`). The expression `Number(options.vadThreshold) || undefined` was written to convert empty/unset input into `undefined` so the downstream realtime library picks its own default. However, `Number("0")` is `0`, and `0 || undefined` evaluates to `undefined` because `0` is falsy in JavaScript. The `||` operator cannot distinguish "user typed nothing" from "user typed 0" — both produce the same falsy numeric result — so both cases are mapped to `undefined`.

The fix checks the trimmed string directly: `options.vadThreshold.trim() ? Number(options.vadThreshold) : undefined`. An empty/whitespace-only string is falsy and falls through to `undefined`; the string `"0"` is truthy and correctly becomes `Number("0")` → `0`.
